data.name: Jyotish
data.gender_notes: Jyotish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who knows or studies the stars and planets; a term for an astrologer in Indian culture. Derived from the Sanskrit root 'jyoti' meaning 'light' or 'knowledge'. The name Jyotish carries the meaning “God of Astronomy” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jyotish usually hope their child will grow to embody god of astronomy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes wisdom, guidance, and enlightenment through the study of celestial bodies.
data.etymology: Jyotish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Astronomy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jyotish total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Jyotish is a crucial and respected part of Hindu cultural practices. Astrology, or the knowledge of the stars and planets, has been an essential component of Indian life for thousands of years. It is not just used for predicting future events, as commonly believed, but also for guiding important life decisions, such as marriage, starting a business, or even choosing a house or a city to live in. Jyotish is intricately linked to Hindu mythology, religion, and folklore. It is mentioned in numerous Hindu scriptures, including the Vedas and the Puranas.
data.spiritual_significance: Jyotish holds deep spiritual significance in Hindu beliefs. It is believed that the stars and planets influence our lives in mysterious ways and that understanding this influence can bring us closer to our inner selves and the cosmic consciousness. Therefore, Jyotish is considered a tool for self-realization and spiritual growth. It can help us understand the past, present, and future phases of our lives and enable us to make informed decisions. Moreover, it can give us insights into the deeper workings of the universe and help us establish a harmonious and balanced existence. In essence, Jyotish is a bridge between the material and the spiritual worlds, a way to connect with the infinite universe and tap into its divine wisdom.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jyotish: The radiant one, embodiment of knowledge relating to the movements and positions of celestial bodies, guiding the spiritual journey.

historical_references.reference: Jyotish is an ancient Indian science dealing with the study of planets and stars to predict future events and trends.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Jyotish remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Priya Jyotish in Bali, Indonesia attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Jyotish, which means "God of Astronomy". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
